title: FleetHub - Core
description: Connection and integration settings for FleetHub. Preference domain: com.herojoneslabs.fleethub.core — deploy as its own Jamf Pro Application & Custom Settings profile, scoped to all Macs running FleetHub. Holds ONLY non-secret connection settings (no profile ever carries a secret; secrets are entered in the app and stored in the Keychain): Jamf Pro server + master client identity, optional ABM / Jamf Protect / Entra integrations, sign-in method, and local administration. Values override in-app Settings and take effect at app relaunch.

configurationVersion.title: Configuration Version
configurationVersion.description: Schema version for compatibility checking (informational — the loader logs it, nothing else reads it)

jamfPro.title: Jamf Pro Connection
jamfPro.description: Jamf Pro server connection and master API client identity. serverURL is always required. masterClientID is required on the Jamf Pro API backend, where the master client only creates each person's own API client; it is unused on the Platform API backend. The matching client secret is never delivered by a profile: it is kept in the Keychain, entered in the app (first-run setup or Settings > Credentials) or delivered by the credential import policy.

serverURL.title: Jamf Pro Server URL
serverURL.description: Full HTTPS base URL, no trailing slash. e.g. https://yourorg.jamfcloud.com

masterClientID.title: Master API Client ID
masterClientID.description: OAuth client_id of the master Jamf API client used by FleetHub. Not secret. The paired client_secret is NEVER delivered by a profile: operators enter it in the app (first-run onboarding or Settings → Credentials) and it is stored in the Keychain.

requiredRoleName.title: Required Jamf API Role Name
requiredRoleName.description: DEFAULT Jamf API Role attached to a person's own API client when their role in the Access profile does not name one (Access > roles > Jamf API Role Name). Every app function runs as that client. With per-role names set for every role this is only a fallback; if neither is set, sign-in fails closed with a clear message. The app has no built-in default.

userCredentialLifetimeDays.title: User Credential Lifetime (days)
userCredentialLifetimeDays.description: Lifetime of per-user Jamf API client credentials provisioned by the app; expiry forces re-provisioning. Clamped 1-365.

eraseAckTimeoutSeconds.title: Erase Acknowledgment Timeout (seconds)
eraseAckTimeoutSeconds.description: How long every erase (Erase Device / Return to Service) waits for the device to acknowledge the ERASE_DEVICE command. Cleanup steps (Jamf record delete, Entra object delete) NEVER run without acknowledgment — on timeout the flow stops. Clamped 30-1800.

eraseAckPollIntervalSeconds.title: Erase Acknowledgment Poll Interval (seconds)
eraseAckPollIntervalSeconds.description: How often the app polls Jamf Pro for the ERASE_DEVICE acknowledgment while waiting. Clamped 5-120.

apiBackend.title: API Backend
apiBackend.description: Which API FleetHub talks to. 'jamfPro' (default): the Jamf Pro API on your tenant URL — each operator gets their own API client, so Jamf's audit log names the person. 'hybrid': READS (Overview, search, device details, reports, My Devices) go through the Jamf Platform API gateway as the single integration described in Platform API Integration below, while every ACTION and anything gated or sensitive (MDM commands, wipe and Return to Service, local admin password, FileVault key, Screen Share sign-in, Move to Site, PreStage, Cleanup, DDM status) still runs on the Jamf Pro API as the operator's own client, so Jamf's audit names the person. Needs BOTH the Platform integration and the master (provisioning) client. 'platform': everything goes through the gateway as that one integration. The Platform API has no per-user API clients, so on this backend every operator on the Mac acts as the integration: Jamf's audit names the integration, and FleetHub's own action log is what names the person. 'hybrid' and 'platform' require Platform API Integration to be filled in (including the Tenant ID); if it is incomplete, calls fail with a clear 'not configured' error rather than falling back.

platformAPI.title: Platform API Integration
platformAPI.description: Identity of a Jamf Platform API integration created in Jamf Account (account.jamf.com > APIs > Create Credential). NON-SECRET values only: the client secret is NEVER delivered by a profile — operators enter it in the app (first-run onboarding or Settings → Credentials) and it is stored in the Keychain. Filling this in while API Backend stays 'jamfPro' enables Compliance Benchmarks only (they exist solely on the Platform API); setting API Backend to 'platform' additionally routes every Jamf call through the gateway. Integrations expire six months after creation and must be renewed in Jamf Account.

region.title: Region
region.description: Gateway region the integration was created in. Tokens are region-locked: a credential from one region is rejected by another. An unrecognized value leaves the integration unconfigured.

clientID.title: Client ID
clientID.description: The integration's client ID from Jamf Account (Credentials > Get Credentials). Not secret.

tenantID.title: Tenant ID
tenantID.description: UUID of your Jamf Pro instance, from the Integration details panel in Jamf Account. Sent as X-Tenant-Id on Jamf Pro calls made through the gateway. Required when API Backend is 'platform'.

environmentID.title: Environment ID
environmentID.description: UUID of the platform environment, from the Integration details panel in Jamf Account. Sent as X-Environment-Id on Compliance Benchmarks and device lookups. Required for Compliance Benchmarks.

protectTenantID.title: Jamf Protect Tenant ID
protectTenantID.description: UUID of your Jamf PROTECT tenant, from the Integration details panel in Jamf Account. Sent as X-Tenant-Id on Jamf Protect calls made through the gateway. This is NOT the Jamf Pro Tenant ID: each product instance has its own. Needed for Jamf Protect through the Platform API; if empty, the Environment ID is used instead, which Jamf may refuse for Protect.

appleBusinessManager.title: Apple Business Manager (optional)
appleBusinessManager.description: Optional Apple Business Manager API connection — omit entirely if unused. The private key is never delivered by a profile: it is entered in Settings > Credentials and kept in the Keychain. ABM is configured only when clientID, keyID, and that key are all present.

enabled.title: Enable ABM
enabled.description: Enable the Apple Business Manager integration. Absent key means disabled.

clientID.title: ABM API Client ID
clientID.description: Apple Business Manager API client identifier. Not secret.

keyID.title: ABM Key ID
keyID.description: Key ID of the ABM API private key. Not secret — the PEM itself is entered in the app (Settings → Credentials) and stored in the Keychain, never in a profile.

serviceType.title: Apple Service Type
serviceType.description: Which Apple service hosts your organization: business (Apple Business Manager, api-business.apple.com) or school (Apple School Manager, api-school.apple.com). Same API and token flow.

defaultMdmServerName.title: ABM Lookup — Default MDM Server Filter
defaultMdmServerName.description: Preselect the ABM Lookup server filter to this MDM server name (case-insensitive match). A starting point the operator can change — not a lock. No match = 'Any Server'.

defaultDeviceType.title: ABM Lookup — Default Device Type Filter
defaultDeviceType.description: Preselect the ABM Lookup device-type filter. A starting point the operator can change. Unrecognized values fall back to 'all'.

jamfProtect.title: Jamf Protect (optional)
jamfProtect.description: Optional Jamf Protect support for the Cleanup feature — omit entirely if unused. When a Platform API Integration with a Jamf Protect Tenant ID (or an Environment ID) is configured, Protect requests go through it (the integration needs devices:read, plus devices:delete to remove records) and only 'enabled' is needed here. Without one, give the Protect tenant URL and API client ID; that client's password is never delivered by a profile: it is entered in Settings > Credentials and kept in the Keychain.

enabled.title: Enable Jamf Protect
enabled.description: Enable the Jamf Protect integration. Absent key means disabled.

url.title: Jamf Protect Tenant URL
url.description: Full HTTPS tenant URL. e.g. https://yourorg.protect.jamfcloud.com

clientID.title: Jamf Protect API Client ID
clientID.description: Jamf Protect API client identifier. Not secret.

entra.title: Microsoft Entra Device Cleanup (optional)
entra.description: Optional Entra (Graph) cleanup for Return to Service — deletes the erased Mac's Entra device object(s) so it can re-register cleanly. Omit to disable. Carries ONLY the non-secret identity of the app registration; its client secret or certificate PEM is entered in the app (Settings → Credentials) and stored in the Keychain, never in a profile. The app registration needs Device.ReadWrite.All plus the Cloud Device Administrator role.

tenantID.title: Tenant ID
tenantID.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID (GUID). Not secret.

clientID.title: Client ID
clientID.description: Entra app registration (client) ID (GUID). Not secret.

cloudInstance.title: Azure Cloud Instance
cloudInstance.description: Azure cloud for the Entra cleanup flow: global (login.microsoftonline.com / graph.microsoft.com), usgov (Azure Government / GCC High), or china (Azure operated by 21Vianet).

signIn.title: Interactive Sign-In (optional)
signIn.description: How users sign into FleetHub — identity only; it grants no capabilities (those live in the access domain's roles block). Omit to keep the built-in email sign-in flow. Distinct from the entra block above, which is app-only Graph cleanup credentials. FAIL-CLOSED: method=entra with missing tenant/client ids blocks sign-in rather than falling back to email.

method.title: Sign-In Method
method.description: How people sign in. entra = Microsoft Entra ID only: the login screen shows a single Sign In with Microsoft button, email sign-in is turned off, and role names come from the roles in the person's sign-in. email = a typed work email address with no identity provider, and the role named by the access profile's role key; use it only where no Entra sign-in is configured. If the Entra ID Sign-In block below carries a tenant ID and client ID, FleetHub uses Entra and turns email sign-in off even when this is left as email.

entra.title: Entra ID Sign-In
entra.description: Entra ID interactive sign-in settings. Use a separate PUBLIC-client app registration (no client secret — none is needed or used). Role capabilities are defined in the access domain, not here; a user whose token roles match no access-domain entry is refused sign-in (fail-closed). Also enable 'Assignment required' on the enterprise application Entra-side — client-side checks are a UX gate, not a security boundary.

tenantId.title: Tenant ID
tenantId.description: Directory (tenant) ID GUID. Required when method=entra. The aliases 'common' and 'organizations' are NOT supported — issuer validation is tenant-specific. Set the real value in Jamf; never commit it to a repo.

clientId.title: Client ID (public client)
clientId.description: Application (client) id of the public-client app registration. Not secret. Required when method=entra.

cloudInstance.title: Azure Cloud Instance
cloudInstance.description: Azure cloud for interactive sign-in: global (login.microsoftonline.com), usgov (Azure Government / GCC High), or china (Azure operated by 21Vianet). Same mapping as entra.cloudInstance above — both Entra features agree on hosts per cloud.

redirectURI.title: Redirect URI (optional)
redirectURI.description: Only when your app registration uses a redirect URI other than the default, fleethubauth://callback. Enter it exactly as registered under Mobile and desktop applications; a mismatch fails sign-in with AADSTS50011. Must be a custom-scheme URI such as myapp://callback, not http or https. Leave unset to use the default.

allowedGroupIds.title: Allowed Group IDs (optional)
allowedGroupIds.description: Optional extra check: the signed-in user must belong to at least one of these Entra group object ids (GUIDs), via the token's groups claim. Empty = no check. Caveat: users in many groups get an overage token with no groups listed and will fail this check — prefer app roles, which never overage.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: Sign-in behavior preferences, enforced in the sign-in and session views. Moved here from the ui domain — a ui profile still delivering this block is honored until you re-push, but core wins when both are present.

requireBiometric.title: Require Biometric
requireBiometric.description: Require Touch ID / biometric authentication to use the app.

allowBiometricSetup.title: Allow Biometric Setup
allowBiometricSetup.description: Allow users to enable biometric unlock in-app.

sessionTimeout.title: Session Timeout (min, 0 = none)
sessionTimeout.description: Idle session timeout in minutes. 0 disables the timeout.

allowRememberMe.title: Allow Remember Me
allowRememberMe.description: Allow the sign-in screen to remember the last operator.

autoCreateUserApiClient.title: Create Per-User API Clients Automatically
autoCreateUserApiClient.description: Off (default): FleetHub creates nothing in Jamf and needs no provisioning client or secret. A Jamf administrator creates each operator's API client and attaches its API role; the operator enters the client ID and secret in FleetHub once, where it is checked with Jamf and kept in their Keychain. On: FleetHub creates a Jamf API client for each operator at first sign-in, using the provisioning (master) client named above, and keeps its role in step with their FleetHub role. That needs the provisioning client's secret in each operator's Keychain, and it needs Microsoft Entra ID sign-in: email sign-in is refused while this is on. Off is the more secure choice, because a provisioning secret can create an API client with any API role. Either way, every app function runs as the operator's own client and fails closed without one.
